articles.title: Kevin Pietersen: Former England batter on Harry Brook and working with Test side before Ashes
articles.summary: Former batter turned specialist mentor Kevin Pietersen talks about his new role with England, his past history with the ECB and working with Harry Brook and Brendon McCullum.
articles.body:
Kevin Pietersen is asked, after everything that came before, what he would have said if told he would work for the England and Wales Cricket board again one day.

In 2014, he was sacked by the ECB in one of most ugly and acrimonious periods in English cricketing history – a period that brought one of the most exciting but divisive international careers to an end.

"What do you think I'd have said," Pietersen says with a smile.

Bigger stars in English cricket are harder to find.

This is the man who had a brief but high-profile relationship with American celebrity Caprice, married a pop star, Jessica from Liberty X, and once tried to explain cricket to Taylor Swift on The Graham Norton Show.

Back in the dressing room as a mentor, he is speaking to the media at Headingley - the location of his famous "it's tough being me" press conference.

The hair is greyer, but he still carries all of that aura.

"I'm 46, man," he says, asked whether animosity remains.

"That stuff is so long gone. I am a completely different person.

"I live in South Africa. I love doing what I do. I am just here to help Brendon first and foremost, help the players try and become the best versions of themselves."

Listen to Pietersen's interview with Test Match Special

My preconceptions of England 'completely different' to reality

Pietersen was the most intriguing of appointments to England's dressing room staff because of his own history, but also what he has said before.

While commentating on England's white-ball tour of India last year, he suggested the Brendon McCullum outfit were not training enough.

"Clearly the perceptions I had before being asked to do the job were completely different to what I feel now," he says.

"It is nice to being part of an England team and set-up that is actually really, really driven."

Pietersen answers every question with poise. Almost all are given and lengthy, considered responses.

His only terse response comes when pushed on what exactly those preconceptions were - and how quickly they took to disappear.

"You know what the preconceptions were," he says. "I am not going near it."

I can help these players 'stay away from the ugly'

Despite that, he appears to be loving his return.

Pietersen is "not sitting here wanting to be the coach of England" but wants to help McCullum and the players, many of whom grew up idolising him.

One of those, Tom Banton, said last week he is still in awe of the four-time Ashes-winner, so much so he was struggling to build up the courage to speak to him.

"He wants a YouTube channel," Pietersen laughs. Pietersen, a 50-over great who played in a way ahead of his time, can also help him there.

His official title is "specialist mentor" and he will dip in and out to work with the white-ball teams through to the 50-over World Cup next autumn.

Before the first ODI in Durham, England posted a clip on social media of Pietersen leading a batting session.

Holding court, he had Joe Root and Rehan Ahmed alike involved in a batting drill on how to rotate the strike against spin.

"All I want to be is a great person to these guys," Pietersen says.

"I want to be the best guy in the room, so that they come to me, and they ask me for information, and if I've got stuff for them, I'll give it to them.

"I am lucky to have worn every T-shirt an England cricketer can wear – the good, the bad the ugly.

"I can potentially help them to stay away from the ugly."

Pietersen's eyes roll slightly when he is asked about Ben Stokes' recent comments comparing Harry Brook's talents to his.

Pietersen, like Brook, was a maverick – a batter capable of incredible highs. Those highs mean the lows come with a disproportionate level of criticism.

"Where I can help him is playing situations, because there was a lot of method in my madness," Pietersen says.

"Yes, occasionally, I got out to reckless shots and crazy shots in the '80s and '90s but there was a lot of structure to the way that I batted.

"I've still got notes on my phone on how I played in T20 cricket, one-day cricket, Test match cricket, and about hitting straight back at the stumps, and the techniques, and how I did it, and don't play certain shots.

"That all-round structure is something I could potentially help him with because he's so flipping good.

"It's actually frightening how good he is and how good he can be."

And Pietersen says he will not limit himself to working purely on white-ball cricket.

He has already spoken to new Test coach Stephen Fleming about how he can help the Test batters during his time with the white-ball squads.

Though he said he would not have time for a full-time role, he suggested he is open to working with the Test side before next summer's home Ashes series.

"I have got a pretty mad schedule," he says. "I wouldn't say no.

"I don't think that necessarily means I need to be in a dressing room.

"There is a lot of time in the lead up to an Ashes series and a tour of South Africa, when I will be with the Test batters.

"There are conversations I can have there."

Who knows how long this will last. England may as well make the most of this second chance.

articles.title: Kevin Pietersen says he is "completely different person" after taking England role and hints at role ahead of Ashes
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen says he "wouldn't say no" to the opportunity to contribute to England's coaching team for next year's Ashes against Australia; Pietersen recently made a surprise return to the England set-up as a specialist on the white-ball coaching staff
articles.body:
Pietersen represented England 277 times across all formats during his playing days, but was sacked in 2014 and has since been disconnected from the side for more than a decade after the ECB accused him of failing to support captain Sir Alastair Cook following the 5-0 Ashes defeat in Australia.

He was also dropped in 2012 after sending texts to the South African team, and since retiring has been a vocal critic of England, accusing the white-ball team of poor preparation ahead of last January's tour of India.

Having recently returned to the England set up as a specialist on the white-ball coaching staff, Pietersen is keen to offer his talents and experience to the current crop of England stars.

"I'm 46, man. That stuff's so long gone. I'm a completely different person too," he said.

"I've been lucky to have worn every t-shirt an England cricketer can wear; the good, the bad, and the ugly. There are parts to all of their careers, which I think that I could potentially help them to stay away from the ugly.

"I'm in the two ears, one mouth phase. I listen twice as much as I talk. I've seen a lot, I've done a lot, and I want to be the best guy in the room for these guys

"(White ball head coach McCullum) loves being challenged on different opinions. Whether he uses it or not, that's up to him. He is the head coach. I'm not sitting here wanting to be the coach of England. He's the coach of England. If I can help him, in his journey, in his pursuit, in our pursuit, to be competitive next year then it's a win."

Pietersen joined the coaching staff ahead of the ongoing series against Sri Lanka and will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa.

Recalling his first conversation with McCullum, he said: "I thought I was in trouble," he said of his first conversation with Brendon McCullum. "'What have I done now? Why is he calling me?'

"We talked about how critical I had been of the setup. It took a couple of weeks of conversations with him to be able to convince me that it was something that I wanted to do because the perception wasn't actually the reality that I now know, about what is in that dressing room. These guys are really, really driven.

"It's amazing to be back in an England dressing room and it's amazing to be back with these guys. They are very, very eager to learn. They want to be the best versions of themselves."

Pietersen also suggested there is a chance he could contribute to England's red ball activity when new Test coach Stephen Fleming leads his team into next year's Ashes.

"I've got a pretty mad schedule, (but) I wouldn't say no," he explained.

"I have had a conversation with Stephen, but I don't think that necessarily means that I need to be in a dressing room. There's a lot of time in the lead up to an Ashes series. There's a lot of time in the lead up to the tour of South Africa, where I'm going to be with the Test players, the Test batters in Australia, and there's conversations that can be had there.

"I've certainly had conversations with Flem, who I absolutely love, about language that he would like me to use with the Test batters, going into South Africa, and then certainly into the summer next year. I just don't think I can commit to a lot more time."

articles.title: How to watch Canada Super 60 2026 on Dafanews: Live stream, schedule for the T10 cricket tournament
articles.summary: Here's everything you will need to know to stream the Canada Super 60 2026 T10 cricket tournament live on Dafanews.
articles.body:
North America's most explosive short-format cricket tournament returns for its second season, as the Canada Super 60 2026 gets underway at BC Place Stadium in Vancouver, running from September 29 to October 4.

Fronted by Indian great Yuvraj Singh and streamed live on Dafanews, the tournament brings together six men's franchises and three women's sides for six straight days of T10 cricket, the fastest format in the game, alongside live concerts and entertainment at the iconic indoor venue.

Season 2 has expanded on last year's debut, with an international player draft in July bringing in stars including Jonny Bairstow, James Vince, Martin Guptill and Sikandar Raza to line up alongside Canada's own emerging domestic talent.

Meanwhile, the defending champion in the men's division of the Canada Super 60 is the Brampton Blitz. Meanwhile, the Toronto Sixers are the title holders in the women's tournament.

Canada Super 60 2026: Live stream, TV Channel

Live Streaming: Match details and updates of the Canada Super 60 2026 will be on Dafanews.

How to watch: Getting started only takes a couple of minutes. Create a Dafabet account , navigate to the live sports tab, and every fixture becomes available to follow, complete with ball-by-ball scores and updates as they happen.

When is the Canada Super 60? Dates and full schedule

Tournament Duration: The Canada Super 60 2026 runs from September 29 to October 4, across six straight days of cricket.

Match Format: Both the men's and women's competitions run concurrently, with multiple matches scheduled most days at BC Place.

Daily Timings: Matches are staggered throughout the day, typically beginning at 1:30 p.m. local time (PDT), with several fixtures also held at 4:00 p.m., 6:45 p.m. and 10:45 p.m. local time.

Women's Competition: The three-team women's event runs a shorter league phase before an eliminator on October 2 and the final on October 3.

Men's Competition: The six-team men's league phase wraps up ahead of the semifinals and final, all of which will be played on October 4.

Teams in Action: (Men's) Brampton Blitz, Mississauga Masters, Montreal Royal Tigers, Vancouver Anchors, Toronto Sixers and Whiterock Warriors; (Women's) Toronto Sixers Women, Vancouver Warriors Women and Vancouver Anchors Women.

Mississauga Masters vs Vancouver Anchors

Vancouver Anchors vs Montreal Royal Tigers

Whiterock Warriors vs Mississauga Masters

Montreal Royal Tigers vs Mississauga Masters

Montreal Royal Tigers vs Whiterock Warriors

Toronto Sixers Women vs Vancouver Warriors Women

Vancouver Anchors Women vs Toronto Sixers Women

Vancouver Warriors Women vs Vancouver Anchors Women

Women's Final: Team 1 vs Winner of Eliminator

Tournament Structure: Six men's franchises play a round-robin league phase, each side facing the others before the standings are finalised.

Qualification Rules: The top four men's teams advance to the semifinals, with the two winners progressing to the final on October 4. The three-team women's competition sends the top team into the finals while the second and third-placed teams battle it out in the eliminator, with the winner advancing to the final.

Match Rules: Games are played under T10 regulations, with each side facing just 10 overs per innings.

Team Composition: The field mixes marquee international signings with Canadian domestic talent, following a July player draft that saw more than 1,300 players from 34 countries register for a place in the league.

The tournament takes place entirely at BC Place Stadium in Vancouver, British Columbia, with cricket moving indoors at the 42-year-old venue that has previously hosted the 2010 Winter Olympics ceremonies and major concert tours.

The event is organised by Canada Super 60 in partnership with Cricket Canada. Moreover, CBC has separately signed on as a broadcast and streaming partner within Canada, reflecting the league's growing push to establish T10 cricket as a mainstream product in North America.

articles.title: Jos Buttler ruled out of England's third ODI vs Sri Lanka with injury as Surrey's Dan Lawrence called into squad
articles.summary: Jos Buttler is out of England’s third ODI against Sri Lanka after suffering a hamstring injury in the defeat at Headingley; Dan Lawrence has been called up; watch the third and final ODI live on Sunday from 10am live on Sky Sports Cricket (first ball 10.30am)
articles.body:
An ECB spokesperson said: "Surrey batter Dan Lawrence has been called into the England Men's squad for Sunday's third Metro Bank ODI against Sri Lanka.

"Jos Buttler has been ruled out due to the hamstring injury he suffered in the second Metro Bank ODI at Headingley last night [Thursday] and will undergo further assessment."

Lawrence has been withdrawn from Surrey's County Championship fixture against Somerset and is set to train with England at The Oval on Saturday morning.

Sri Lanka showed great fight to halt the hosts' chase in the second ODI and secure a 16-run victory at Headingley, levelling the three-match series at 1-1. Buttler played a decisive role in the hosts' chase before his injury ruled him out of the series decider.

Buttler had looked set to guide the hosts towards victory before pulling up in the 38th over with England 254-4. He was forced to retire hurt but returned to the crease in the 48th over in a final attempt to rescue the chase. Despite the injury, he went on to make 69 before being dismissed.

Will Jacks (52), Rehan Ahmed (0), Gus Atkinson (16) and Jamie Overton (2) also fell as the hosts' hopes faded. England managed just one four and one six from the 37th over onwards as Sri Lanka's bowlers tightened the pressure to seal a hard-fought win.

With the series finely poised at 1-1, the hosts must now regroup for the decider without Buttler, who played a central role in their second ODI chase.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Hardik Pandya's return to competitive cricket has been delayed again as the all-rounder is set to miss the three India A fixtures against
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Hardik Pandya's return to competitive cricket has been delayed again as the all-rounder is set to miss the three India A fixtures against Australia A in Puducherry starting October 6. The all-rounder experienced pain in his right shin again earlier this week and underwent a fresh set of scans. The BCCI medical team monitoring him has advised further rest.The 32-year-old was inching closer to a return to cricket but the recurring shin issue has derailed all the progress he made at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in the last few months.It was the same issue that ruled him out of selection for the Afghanistan T20Is. It is understood that he was also being considered for a late entry into the Asian Games but the unfortunate turn of events occurred close to selection day - first before the Afghanistan ODIs and then later for the T20Is against the same opposition.With no physical activity for the next 10-15 days, it remains highly doubtful that Pandya will be available for the T20Is against New Zealand next month as well. The selectors would also operate with caution when considering him directly for the ODIs which follow the five T20Is. The team management's frustrating wait for their premier all-rounder continues, but they understand that a rushed approach will not be followed as the 2027 World Cup remains the ultimate goal.There is no official word from the Indian cricket board yet. articles.title: County Championship: Hain ton edges Bears nearer to 2026 title
articles.summary: Centurion Sam Hain shares a 165-run stand with skipper Ed Barnard against Leicestershire to edge Warwickshire close to a ninth County Championship title.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Edgbaston (day two)

Leicestershire 125 & 55-3: Budinger 43*; Bamber 2-27

Warwickshire 372: Hain 142, Barnard 88; A Patel 3-78

Leicestershire (3 pts) trail Warwickshire (6 pts) by 192 runs

Sam Hain hit a splendid day two century against relegation-threatened Leicestershire at Edgbaston to keep Warwickshire on course to win a ninth County Championship title.

In seamer-friendly conditions, Hain compiled a highly-skilled 142 from 301 balls - his 21st century in first-class cricket - as the Bears reached 372 to take a substantial first-innings lead of 247.

Hain, who reached his 1,000 first-class runs for the season, for only the second time, was well supported by Ed Barnard who made 88 in a partnership of 165 in 50 overs.

Leicestershire, rolled for 125 first time round, then closed on 55-3 after Bears paceman Ethan Bamber took two more wickets to take his season's tally to 66.

A draw would now be enough to secure the title but the home supporters, who have turned out in force on the first two days, will arrive for the third expecting a fourth to be unnecessary.

Foxes relegated by Bears, subject to points appeal

Championship titles are constructed on a bedrock of solid sessions interspersed with the occasional spectacular one - and Hain and Barnard's efforts were the epitome of solid.

Resuming on 130-4, already five runs in front, they added 51 without loss in a morning session truncated by bad light.

Hain and Barnard did exactly what their team required, advancing steadily to lay the platform for a big lead and potential innings victory.

The Bears' fifth-wicket pair continued to concentrate hard after lunch until, with the lead already 126, Barnard departed livid with himself at edging a big drive at a wide ball from Ben Green - just 12 shy of a century.

Chris Woakes chipped his second ball to mid-on, but Kai Smith and Manny Suthar enjoyed useful cameos before also falling to the persevering Hull.

They had accompanied the excellent Hain towards his century which was greeted by a standing ovation from the big audience, then Bamber added further useful runs before being bowled by a beauty from Patel.

Even then the Foxes' frustration went on as last pair Hain and Olly Hannon-Dalby added 35.

Leicestershire opener Sol Budinger then came out firing, hitting 43 not out off 36 balls, But Bamber struck twice in three balls, trapping Sheridon Gumbs and then flattening Rishi Patel's off-stump two balls late.

After a bad-light interruption, Woakes then pinned Steve Eskinazi lbw in the gloom to leave Warwickshire maybe only one strong session away from the title.
